messages.author: e14ab5843c32249d
messages.subject: Troubleshooting FragPipe input to dataProcess
parts:
Hi all,
Thanks for putting out and maintaining a package so well. I am extremely new to MSstats so forgive the naive question. I have searched previous issues and while they are somewhat similar I couldnt find one with this specific issue. If I missed something please just point me towards it if you could!

I have, hopefully, a fairly simple problem with FragPipe output being fed to dataProcess. This was from an exploratory label-free DDA experiment. Experimental setup is
  • No bio or tech reps per condition
  • 3 fractions per condition
  • Lots of different conditions, lots of missing values due to tissue source differences
Here is screenshot of the input data (slightly modified from initial FragPipe output due to issue listed below):

So with the MSstats.csv in hand, I do the following:
  1. Take output from FragPipe and run it through FragPipetoMSstatsFormat()
  2. Complains there might be fractions (there are) or tech reps (there are NOT)
    1. "** MSstats suspects that there are fractionations and potentially technical replicates too. Please add Fraction column to the input."
  3. Add Fraction column with fraction numbers (as seen in screeenshot)
  4. Finishes FragPipetoMSstatsFormat() BUT with lots of "Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf" messages - possibly due to NAs?
  5. Feed output to dataProcess() and  get following error:
    "Error in merge.data.table(input[, colnames(input) != "newABUNDANCE", with = FALSE], : Elements listed in `by` must be valid column names in x and y" Which seems to suggest it is trying to generate a df without matching columns.
    1. Here is traceback:


However, if I change all fraction numbers to 1 (not correct, as these were fractions) it seems to assume files are tech reps and dataProcess() will finish generating the dataProcess() object/list. 

I've tried several other things such as making the file smaller to test if it's a memory issue (doesn't seem to be). I've also confirmed the test DDA set included with MSstats runs normally. It seems clear it may be an issue with feature metadata formatting for this dataset but I am scratching my head as to why, when including the correct fraction number causes it to error out. Maybe MSstats is expecting more replicates or I am missing a setting change? But the test DDA dataset is fairly simple and doesn't have any replicates so I suppose it should be ok. Any insight is appreciated!

Cheers
Carlos
